releases.notes:
# Features

- Added optional "warning" vibrations before each shock
- Added an option to allow other mods to bypass limits (mostly theoretical right now as I don't think there are any such mods :sweat_smile: you'll know when you need it though)
- Added an option to toggle shocks from damage/gameplay (again, mostly theoretical; this disables the only way this mod has of generating shocks by itself, but might be useful if you want to play with a mod that hooks into this without also receiving shocks for ingame damage)

# Improvements

- Config file is slightly more human readable
- Tidied some of the config options ever so slightly
- Made duration sliders in the config menu increase in steps of 0.05 seconds, rather than 0.001 seconds, because it's easier to get nice and satisfying numbers from that lol (you can still make precise edits if you edit the json file)

# Fixes

- Some edge cases around serial port reuse are fixed
- Made serial port connection test timeouts more robust
- Made modmenu *actually* optional (previously `/pishock-zap config` required modmenu)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ScoreUnder/pishock-zap-fabric/compare/v2.3.2...v2.4.0

releases.notes:
# v2.0.0 for Minecraft 1.20

## New features

- Public-facing API for other mods to consume! See [the `PishockZapApi` class](https://github.com/ScoreUnder/pishock-zap-fabric/blob/v2.0.0+1.20/src/main/java/moe/score/pishockzap/PishockZapApi.java)
- PiShock WebSocket API backend (newer, faster one)
- OpenShock APIs too (yes, really)
  - The serial one is only half-implemented, forgive me!

## Improvements

- Batch up serial operations
- Bring along some auto-config buttons into the menu (these were genuinely awful to hack in lol)

## Cleanup

- Deprecate PiShock Web v1 API (doesn't work any more :( )
- Refactor shock backends to conform to a common interface
- Decouple a few internals from PiShock Web V1 API stuff

## Full changelog

https://github.com/ScoreUnder/pishock-zap-fabric/compare/v1.3.0+1.20...v2.0.0+1.20
